editorialPolicy.storyFidelity: Each level preserves the complete event sequence, motivations, consequence, and chapter ending.
editorialPolicy.foundation: Concrete 6–11 word sentences, one main action per line, minimal subordinate clauses.
editorialPolicy.core: Connected 10–18 word sentences with cause, contrast, and reaction.
editorialPolicy.studio: Literary but speakable sentences that preserve narrator wit, suspense, and moral tension.
editorialPolicy.safety: Historic slapstick and peril are described without adding graphic detail. Harmful actions retain their consequences and are not presented as desirable.
editorialPolicy.narration: Dialogue is acted with restraint inside one continuous chapter-level performance; no independent sentence generations.

narration.direction: Make the reunion exuberant and musical, then cut the warmth sharply when Fire Eater appears. His threat should feel theatrical and frightening without becoming graphic.
narration.productionRule: Generate one continuous master per level and derive sentence timestamps from that same master.

lines.text: Pinocchio entered the crowded puppet theater.
The wooden actors recognized him as a brother.
They stopped the play and cheered loudly.
Pinocchio jumped onto the stage with them.
Then the frightening director appeared.
His name was Fire Eater.
He needed more wood for his cooking fire.
Fire Eater ordered the puppets to bring Pinocchio.

lines.text: Pinocchio slipped inside while Harlequin and Pulcinella performed onstage.
The wooden actors suddenly recognized him and called him their brother.
Their joyful welcome stopped the play and angered the waiting audience.
Pinocchio leaped across the seats and joined the celebration onstage.
The noise ended when the theater's enormous director appeared.
Fire Eater had a black beard, burning eyes, and a dangerous whip.
After the show, he went to the kitchen where a lamb cooked over a fire.
Because the fire needed wood, he remembered the newly arrived marionette.
He ordered Harlequin and Pulcinella to carry Pinocchio into the kitchen.
Terrified, Pinocchio cried for Geppetto and begged not to die.

lines.text: Pinocchio entered the theater while Harlequin and Pulcinella exchanged their usual comic threats beneath the stage lights.
The performance stopped the instant the wooden actors recognized a living marionette among the spectators.
Calling him their brother, the entire company abandoned the script and invited Pinocchio into a thunderous reunion.
He bounded from audience to orchestra to stage, where the delighted troupe carried him around in triumph.
The celebration vanished when the director emerged with a floor-length black beard, glowing eyes, and an enormous whip.
Fire Eater's presence reduced the noisy theater to a silence so complete that even a passing fly might be heard.
When the show ended, the director returned to a kitchen where his supper still turned above an underfed fire.
Needing seasoned wood, he decided that the unexpected marionette would make excellent fuel.
Harlequin and Pulcinella obeyed in fear and carried their struggling new brother toward the fire.
The chapter closes with Pinocchio calling desperately for the father whose gift he had abandoned.
